To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

damage to the TPJs, the middle frontal gyri and the posterior IPS is associated with neglect, that the latter region is a significant predictor of contralesional target detection and the capture of attention by ipsilesional distracter stimuli, and that damage to the FFE and posterior IPS is negatively correlated with the degree of capture of attention by distracters.

the attentional network of the human right hemisphere comprises the intraparietalsulcus (IPS), the dorsal premotor area (PMd) including the frontal eye field (FEF) and the temporal-parieto-occipital junction (TPJ).

(a) the IPS and the dorsal premotor area including the FEF are critical for the selection of relevant environmental events, and for reorienting attention; (b) the IPS is also important for the selection of irrelevant events that capture attention; and (c) the TPJ is critical for the selection and processing of irrelevant environmental stimuli that capture attention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional organization of the human brain and the relationship of this organization to the cognitive and behavioural deficits observed in stroke patients.
the question how the human brain solves a basic task of everyday life, i.e. how the brain selects relevant environmental stimuli and reorients attention to them.
the neural correlates of spatial attention in the human brain and the functional role of the intraparital sulcus, the temporal-parieal junction and the frontal eye fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neglect is associated with damage to a network of brain areas that are functionally related to spatial attention.
damage to the dorsal premotor and parietal cortices (including IPS, FEF, TPJ and superior temporal gyrus) causes neglect.
the attention system is not a unitary entity but rather a network of interconnected areas, and the IPS, dorsal premotor cortex and TPJ are the key areas for attentional orienting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IPS is the most important structure in the attention network of the brain.
the attention network consists of at least three major components: the intraparietale sulcus, the frontal eye field, and the temporal-parietale junction.
the attention network of the brain is a network of networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the network of brain regions involved in the spatial attentional system is more extensive than what has been proposed by lesion-overlap studies, and that the IPS is not only involved in the reorienting but also in the selection of spatial attention.
damage to the IPS, in particular to the posterior part of this region, is critical to the emergence of spatial neglect.
there is a clear dissociation between the neural structures that are damaged in neglect patients and the structures activated in healthy subjects during the performance of spatial attention tasks.
